option: 1. Machined 6061 through-frame + bolted floor plate (the design now)
body_cost_usd: 3,896 at BYU (stock $2,278 + 24.9 h x $65); outside: floor $83.68 (JLCCNC), frame manual quote (estimate $400-1,500), US job shop $4,000-10,000 (Edison r5)
lead_time: 3-4 days on the VF-4 inside the shop queue; JLCCNC 6-7 days + 2-4 days UPS
in_house_h: 24.9 (frame 16.2 + floor 8.7); CAM for both is already programmed and simulated (machining.md round 6)
vacuum_o2: designed for it: 1 mbar holds, rate of rise < 1e-3 mbar/min; 1-2 ppm O2 in theory after 3 cycles (vacuum-and-purge.md)
risk: low: programs checked in CAMotics and for holder collisions; one more face seal (the floor O-ring)

option: 2a. Printed 316L by LPBF, frame + floor as one body, seal faces, bores and threads machined after
body_cost_usd: $4,826.37 (JLC3DP live quote, before review) + ~$270 UPS DDP (estimate from its $180-453 shipping lines) + 10-14 h of finishing at BYU; outside the China route: $13-35k in the US (helper's estimate from AMPower rates)
lead_time: 3-day build + review + 2-4 business days UPS: about 1.5-2 weeks (JLC3DP; 'about 5 days production' on its blog)
in_house_h: 10-14 (estimate: CAM 3-4, three setups 4.5, finishing cuts in 316L 2-4, inspect 1); saves 11-15 h
vacuum_o2: more than enough: machined LPBF 316L reaches the 1e-9 mbar.L/s detection limit (Romanescu 2023) and outgasses like wrought 316L (LAL Orsay, IPAC'19); 16 mm walls need no HIP (Edison r7); one seal fewer, so permeation drops 0.45 ppm O2/h
design_changes: add 1-1.5 mm stock on every seal face, bore and datum; stress-relieve on the plate (JLC3DP lists no stress relief: ask); door opening's 220 mm top edge and the horizontal bores need supports or self-supporting shapes; the floor O-ring and its 18 screws go; 21.8 kg instead of 7.4 kg (the VLM tray load, the robot's payload and the module's heat path change)
risk: medium: distortion over 312 mm (+/-0.4 % = +/-1.2 mm as built; Edison: <0.5 mm after stress relief); a sub-surface pore opened by facing a land (helium check after machining); price subject to review; 316L machines slower than 6061
verdict: workable: $1,980 more than machining at $65/h ($5,876 against $3,896) for 11-15 h less shop time

option: 2b. Printed aluminium by LPBF (JLC3DP 'Aluminum 6061'; AlSi10Mg elsewhere), one body, machined after
body_cost_usd: $2,916.58 (JLC3DP live, before review) + shipping; US AlSi10Mg $8-25k (estimate)
vacuum_o2: as 2a: an AlSi10Mg cold-atom chamber with a 2.5 mm skin held < 1e-10 mbar (Cooper et al. 2021)
design_changes: as 2a, at 7.3 kg; check what alloy JLC3DP's 'Aluminum 6061' is (it states 172 W/m.K, 15 % elongation, service <= 150 C: fine for walls that stay under 60 C)
risk: medium: as 2a; a new material at that vendor
verdict: workable: about the same money as machining at $65/h ($3,767 against $3,896) for 13-17 h less shop time; a backup if the VF-4 queue is the bottleneck, after a design-for-AM pass and a first-article helium test

option: 3. DED (wire-arc or laser-wire) 316L walls on a 316L floor plate, machined all over
body_cost_usd: $4,000-12,000 including machining (helper's estimate); Edison $3,000-8,000 + significant machining
in_house_h: no saving: every face is machined from 0.7-1.8 mm of stock per side, in 316L
vacuum_o2: less documented; porosity 0.1-0.5 % (Edison r7): needs a helium test, maybe impregnation
design_changes: near-net walls with stock everywhere; heavy (316L)
risk: high for a one-off: quote-only vendors, rough surface (Ra > 20 um), distortion

option: 4. Welded box from cut plate (316L or 5083), seal faces machined after welding
body_cost_usd: $1,200-3,500 (Edison r7 estimate: plate, cutting, 8-15 h of TIG, post-weld machining); SendCutSend cuts 6061 to 0.75 in., 304/5052 to 0.5 in., 316 to 0.25 in., no 5083; its welding excludes 6061 and is 'not watertight or gas-tight'
lead_time: 2-4 weeks (estimate), plus a qualified welder's queue
in_house_h: about the same as now: 8-15 h welding + the same top, bottom and wall setups after welding (estimate 20-33 h)
vacuum_o2: fine if the welds are sound and helium-tested; Meyer Tool: under 0.5 ft3 with walls of 0.5 in. or more, machining from plate is usually cheapest (this body is 0.23 ft3)
design_changes: corner welds instead of R10 corners; post-weld stress relief; 6061 HAZ drops to ~110 MPa
risk: medium-high: 0.5-2 mm distortion (Edison r3), weld porosity in aluminium, a welder BYU would have to qualify
verdict: no: the same machining plus weld risk (chamber-construction.md option 4)

body_cost_usd: Ideal Vacuum 6 x 12 x 12 in. short cube kit P109160 $4,150.04 (sale; 291 x 291 x 138 mm inside, ~336 x 336 x 184 outside); LACO 12 in. cube with door $5,850; Lesker BX1212S $7,995
in_house_h: 5 of its 6 plates re-machined (door, slots, ports, window, recoater bores): roughly 15-25 h (estimate)
design_changes: nothing fits the 312 x 222 footprint: the gas envelope grows from 6.4 L to ~11.7 L, the VLM tray layout, recoater, gas slots and module port all move; the front door is a full 12 x 12 face
risk: low for the vacuum, high for the redesign

option: 6. Purge-only enclosure (no vacuum): extrusion or sheet with gaskets
body_cost_usd: $500-1,500 for extrusion, panels and gaskets (estimate); the ports, window and recoater bores still need machined plates
in_house_h: 10-15 h (estimate): no glands or Ra 0.8 lands, but the same ports
vacuum_o2: what flow-purged machines reach: EOS M 290 measured 731 +/- 98 ppm in argon; MySint100 0.1 %; TruPrint 1000 <= 3,000 ppm (100 ppm optional); purge-only gloveboxes 0.5 % (Ossila). Flow-purging 11.3 L to 100 ppm takes ~86 L if perfectly mixed, 2-3 times that in practice; no water is pulled out of the powder
design_changes: drop the pump and the 1 mbar requirement; argon 100-250 L a purge and 2-5 L/min while building (SLM 125 2 L/min, Aconity < 5 L/min) against ~20 L of back-fill and ~50 sccm now
risk: process risk, not build risk: hydrogen porosity in aluminium from powder water (Van Cauwenbergh 2019: a vacuum pre-cycle gave 13 +/- 4 ppm H in parts against 45 +/- 11 ppm in the powder)
verdict: no for an aluminium-screening machine; it saves ~10 h and the pump

option: 7. Bolted box of six flat plates, O-rings in every joint
in_house_h: about 28 h (estimate: six plates at ~4.5 h of CAM, setups and inspection each): no saving
vacuum_o2: eight three-way O-ring junctions: the leak risk the frame avoids

option: 8. Casting (A356 sand cast from a printed mould, or investment-cast 316)
body_cost_usd: $4,500-12,000 one-off with a pattern (Edison r7); a printed sand mould ~EUR 450 at EUR 9/L (helper's estimate) + pouring + machining; impregnation $50-200
lead_time: 6-12 weeks (Edison r7 estimate); every foundry is quote-only
in_house_h: about the same machining as now (every face and port)
vacuum_o2: castings are more porous than plate (Meyer Tool): vacuum impregnation and a helium test
design_changes: draft angles, wall thickness for casting
